# LSS: primary Na/K–SBP vs SSaSS benchmark

The two LSS methods are **distinct interventions on distinct populations**, not
interchangeable estimates of the same thing:

- **Na/K–SBP (primary)** models sodium displacement **and** potassium addition
  through SBP, affecting **all four CVD causes**; it applies to whole-population
  (s2) and to NCD-RisC diagnosed/treated hypertensives (s4/s5).
- **SSaSS trial-RR (benchmark)** applies the SSaSS **stroke** relative risks
  (incidence + case fatality) and is valid only for SSaSS-comparable
  (diagnosed/treated HTN) populations — never the whole population.

```{r nak-vs-ssass, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
# Deaths delayed by scenario (impact window) joined to the LSS audit composition,
# for the HTN variants where both methods exist.
dd_lss <- deaths_delayed_by(data.out, by = character(0), years = impact_y1:impact_y2)
dd_lss <- dd_lss[grepl("^lss", as.character(scenario)),
                 .(scenario = as.character(scenario), deaths_delayed)]
# The Scenario-2 uptake sweep (lss_s2_10..50) is shown in full elsewhere; here we
# compare methods, so keep only the representative (highest-coverage) s2 plus the
# HTN-targeted s4/s5 under both methods.
.s2_cmp <- grep("^lss_s2_[0-9]+$", dd_lss$scenario, value = TRUE)
.s2_cmp_rep <- if (length(.s2_cmp)) .s2_cmp[which.max(as.integer(sub("^lss_s2_", "", .s2_cmp)))] else NULL
dd_lss <- dd_lss[!grepl("^lss_s2_[0-9]+$", scenario) | scenario == .s2_cmp_rep]
la <- as.data.table(lss_audit)
la_sc <- la[, .(elig = eligibility_group[1], cov = mean(eligible_pop_share),
                na_disp = mean(sodium_displaced_g), k_add = mean(potassium_added_g),
                dsbp = mean(sbp_delta_combined_mmHg)), by = .(scenario, method)]
cmp <- merge(la_sc, dd_lss, by = "scenario")   # inner: only the scenarios kept above
cmp[, `:=`(Scenario = scenario_labels[scenario])]
setorder(cmp, method, scenario)
cmp_tbl <- cmp[, .(
  Scenario, Method = method, `Eligibility` = elig,
  `Elig. pop share` = fmt_pct(cov, 1),
  `Na displaced (g)` = formatC(na_disp, format = "f", digits = 3),
  `K increase (g)`   = formatC(k_add,   format = "f", digits = 3),
  `Mean ΔSBP (mmHg)` = ifelse(is.na(dsbp), "n/a (trial RR)", formatC(dsbp, format = "f", digits = 2)),
  `Deaths delayed (M)` = ifelse(is.na(deaths_delayed), "n/a", fmt_m(deaths_delayed)))]
kable(cmp_tbl, caption = paste0("Table 3b. LSS Na/K–SBP vs SSaSS trial-RR ",
      "benchmark: eligibility, exposure change, SBP change and deaths delayed ",
      "(", impact_window, "). The methods are NOT identical interventions — they ",
      "differ in pathway (all-CVD SBP vs stroke-only RR) and are shown side by side, ",
      "not merged."),
      align = c("l","l","l", rep("r",5))) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped","hover","condensed"), full_width = TRUE, font_size = 11) |>
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE) |>
  footnote(general = paste0(
    "ΔSBP is 'n/a (trial RR)' for the SSaSS benchmark because its effect is a ",
    "stroke relative risk, not an SBP change. Na displaced / K increase are the ",
    "same composition for both methods; the health effect differs by pathway."))
```

# Benchmarking against the "100 Million Lives Saved" model {#benchmarking}

As an external sanity check, we compare this build's headline result — the
**full package** of sodium policies — against the previous RTSL/UW
**"100 Million Lives Saved"** estimate for a **30% reduction in population
sodium intake**. The previous-model figures are read from
[`data/raw/UWRTSL-100MLives_Output20260204.xlsx`](../data/raw/UWRTSL-100MLives_Output20260204.xlsx)
(sheet `Location And Cause`, intervention `Population Sodium Reduction`). The
comparison is restricted to the **same selected countries** this report models,
so it tracks the country selection automatically.

**This is a contextual comparison, not a like-for-like validation.** The two
estimates are close in construction but *not* equivalent, and we do not adjust
either to force agreement:

- **Exposure change differs.** The previous scenario applies a **uniform 30%
  cut to all population sodium**. The current full package applies each policy's
  documented effect **only to the sodium sources it can reach** (public
  procurement + FOPL + salt targets + fiscal), giving a country-specific
  total-intake reduction (`salteff`) that is generally **well below 30%**. The
  current package is therefore expected to delay **fewer** deaths than a flat
  30% cut — the gap is a feature of the policy-reach logic, not an error.
- **Outcome & causes.** Both report **deaths delayed** relative to a
  no-intervention baseline over the same four CVD causes (IHD, ischemic stroke,
  intracerebral hemorrhage, HHD), so the outcome definition is aligned.
- **Baselines & horizon differ.** The two models use different baseline death
  counts (different populations, age ranges and projection horizons), so we
  report deaths delayed both in **absolute** terms and as a **percent of each
  model's own baseline** — the percent is the more comparable metric. The
  previous model's cumulative horizon is close to, but not identical to, this
  build's `r impact_window` window.
- **Country names** are harmonised onto this model's spellings before matching
  (all ten priority countries match exactly; e.g. `Viet Nam`).

```{r benchmark-compute, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
# ---- Benchmark: current full package vs 100M-Lives 30% sodium reduction ------
# Previous-model results live in the 100 Million Lives Saved workbook, sheet
# "Location And Cause". The comparison row is the "Population Sodium Reduction"
# intervention, which in that model represents the WHO 30%-relative-reduction
# sodium target. We compare it to THIS build's full package (reusing dd_country
# computed above; the model itself is never re-run here).
PREV_XLSX       <- paste0(wd_raw, "UWRTSL-100MLives_Output20260204.xlsx")
PREV_SHEET      <- "Location And Cause"
PREV_SODIUM_INT <- "Population Sodium Reduction"   # = 30% population sodium reduction

# Harmonise previous-model country names onto this model's spellings. The ten
# priority countries already match; this guards other spellings for robustness.
harmonize_prev_location <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  x[x == "Vietnam"]                  <- "Viet Nam"
  x[x == "United States of America"] <- "United States"
  x
}

# Current model: full-package deaths delayed by country over the impact window.
bench_current <- dd_country[, .(location,
                                dd_current   = deaths_delayed,
                                base_current = baseline_dead)]

# Selected countries = whatever the model was run for; the benchmark filters the
# previous-model table to exactly these, so it updates with the selection.
sel_countries <- sort(unique(as.character(bench_current$location)))

benchmark <- tryCatch({
  prev <- as.data.table(readxl::read_excel(PREV_XLSX, sheet = PREV_SHEET))
  prev[, location := harmonize_prev_location(location)]
  prev <- prev[intervention == PREV_SODIUM_INT & location %in% sel_countries,
               .(location,
                 dd_prev   = as.numeric(deaths_delayed),
                 base_prev = as.numeric(baseline_deaths))]
  b <- merge(bench_current, prev, by = "location", all.x = TRUE)
  b[, `:=`(pct_current = dd_current / base_current,
           pct_prev    = dd_prev    / base_prev,
           ratio       = dd_current / dd_prev)]
  setorder(b, -dd_prev)
  b[]
}, error = function(e) {
  message("Benchmark workbook could not be read: ", conditionMessage(e))
  NULL
})

benchmark_available <- !is.null(benchmark) && nrow(benchmark) > 0 &&
  any(!is.na(benchmark$dd_prev))

# Selected-country totals (used inline, in the deck bundle, and for the plot).
if (benchmark_available) {
  bench_cur_tot   <- sum(benchmark$dd_current, na.rm = TRUE)
  bench_prev_tot  <- sum(benchmark$dd_prev,    na.rm = TRUE)
  bench_ratio_tot <- bench_cur_tot / bench_prev_tot
} else {
  bench_cur_tot <- bench_prev_tot <- bench_ratio_tot <- NA_real_
}

# Long form for the grouped bar plot (built once, reused by the deck export).
bench_model_labs <- c(dd_current = "Current full package",
                      dd_prev    = "Previous 30% sodium reduction")
bench_cols <- c(`Current full package`         = "#1f78b4",
                `Previous 30% sodium reduction` = "#b2182b")
if (benchmark_available) {
  bench_long <- melt(benchmark[, .(location, dd_current, dd_prev)],
                     id.vars = "location", variable.name = "model",
                     value.name = "dd")
  bench_long[, model := factor(bench_model_labs[as.character(model)],
                               levels = unname(bench_model_labs))]
  bench_long <- bench_long[!is.na(dd)]
} else {
  bench_long <- NULL
}
```

```{r benchmark-availability-note, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if (!benchmark_available)
  cat("**Benchmark workbook unavailable — the comparison below is skipped.** ",
      "Place `UWRTSL-100MLives_Output20260204.xlsx` in `data/raw/` and re-knit.\n")
```

Over `r impact_window`, across the `r length(sel_countries)` selected countries,
the current **full package** delays **`r fmt_m(bench_cur_tot)` million** CVD
deaths, versus **`r fmt_m(bench_prev_tot)` million** for the previous flat-30%
sodium-reduction scenario — a ratio of about
**`r formatC(bench_ratio_tot, format = "f", digits = 2)`×**. The current
package delivering a smaller total is expected: its source-limited `salteff` is
generally well below a uniform 30% intake cut.

## Benchmark table

```{r benchmark-table, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
if (benchmark_available) {
  bt  <- copy(benchmark)
  setorder(bt, -dd_prev)
  tot <- data.table(
    location     = "Total (selected countries)",
    dd_current   = sum(bt$dd_current,   na.rm = TRUE),
    base_current = sum(bt$base_current, na.rm = TRUE),
    dd_prev      = sum(bt$dd_prev,      na.rm = TRUE),
    base_prev    = sum(bt$base_prev,    na.rm = TRUE))
  tot[, `:=`(pct_current = dd_current / base_current,
             pct_prev    = dd_prev    / base_prev,
             ratio       = dd_current / dd_prev)]
  bt_all <- rbind(bt, tot, fill = TRUE)

  bt_fmt <- bt_all[, .(
    Country                              = location,
    `Current: deaths delayed (M)`        = fmt_m(dd_current, 3),
    `Current: % of baseline`             = fmt_pct(pct_current, 2),
    `Previous 30%: deaths delayed (M)`   = fmt_m(dd_prev, 3),
    `Previous 30%: % of baseline`        = fmt_pct(pct_prev, 2),
    `Current ÷ previous`                 = formatC(ratio, format = "f", digits = 2)
  )]

  kable(bt_fmt,
        caption = paste0("Table 4. Benchmark — current full package vs. the ",
                         "100 Million Lives Saved 30% population sodium-reduction ",
                         "estimate, ", impact_window, ", ", nrow(bt),
                         " selected countries."),
        align = c("l", rep("r", 5))) |>
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                  full_width = TRUE, font_size = 13) |>
    add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Current model (full package)" = 2,
                       "Previous model (30% sodium)" = 2, " " = 1)) |>
    row_spec(0, bold = TRUE) |>
    row_spec(nrow(bt_fmt), bold = TRUE, background = "#eef2f7") |>
    footnote(general = paste0(
      "Previous-model figures: UWRTSL-100MLives_Output20260204.xlsx (sheet ",
      "'Location And Cause', intervention 'Population Sodium Reduction'). ",
      "'% of baseline' is each model's deaths delayed relative to ITS OWN ",
      "baseline CVD deaths, which is the more comparable metric because the ",
      "two models use different baselines and horizons. This is a contextual ",
      "comparison: the previous scenario applies a uniform 30% sodium cut, ",
      "whereas the full package applies source-limited policy effects, so the ",
      "current total is expected to be lower."))
} else {
  cat("Benchmark workbook unavailable; Table 4 skipped.\n")
}
```

## Figure 7 — Deaths delayed by country: full package vs. 30% sodium reduction

```{r benchmark-fig, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
if (benchmark_available) {
  p_bench <- ggplot(bench_long,
                    aes(dd / 1e6, reorder(location, dd), fill = model)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.7, position = position_dodge(width = 0.78)) +
    geom_text(aes(label = fmt_m(dd, 2)), position = position_dodge(width = 0.78),
              hjust = -0.1, size = 2.9) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = bench_cols, name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.16)), labels = comma) +
    labs(title = paste0("Deaths delayed: current full package vs. previous 30% ",
                        "sodium reduction"),
         subtitle = paste0(length(sel_countries), " selected countries; ",
                          impact_window, "; all CVD causes"),
         x = "Deaths delayed (millions)", y = NULL,
         caption = paste0("Previous = 100 Million Lives Saved, 'Population Sodium ",
                          "Reduction' (30% intake cut). Contextual comparison; ",
                          "scenarios and horizons are not fully equivalent.")) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
  print(p_bench)
} else {
  cat("Benchmark workbook unavailable; Figure 7 skipped.\n")
}
```

**Interpretation.** The two models rank the selected countries similarly —
China and India dominate the absolute deaths delayed under both, tracking their
share of the regional CVD burden. The **previous flat-30% scenario delays more
deaths** than the current full package in essentially every country, consistent
with its larger (uniform) exposure change; the current package's benefit is
bounded by how much of each country's sodium its four policies can actually
reach. Where the current package closes much of the gap (a higher
current ÷ previous ratio), local intake is concentrated in the **packaged**
source that FOPL, salt targets and fiscal policy jointly target. Because the
scenarios and horizons are **not fully equivalent**, these numbers should be
read as a **contextual cross-check** on order of magnitude and country ranking,
not as a validation target.

---

# Limitations and interpretation

- **Deaths delayed, not averted (sodium→SBP policies).** For public procurement,
  FOPL, salt targets, fiscal, and the **primary Na/K→SBP LSS** method, case
  fatality is held at baseline, so these lower incidence and shift mortality
  later; cumulative totals depend on the accounting window. Only the optional
  **SSaSS trial-RR benchmark** lowers stroke case fatality (averting, not only
  delaying, some stroke deaths).
- **NCD-RisC eligibility is age-standardised 30–79, not age-specific.** The
  diagnosed/treated population shares that size LSS scenarios 4/5 are single
  age-standardised values applied across all modelled ages, and the **post-2019
  proportions are carried forward** unchanged. This misstates eligibility at the
  age extremes and ignores any post-2019 diagnosis/treatment gains.
- **LSS uptake and adherence are uncertain.** Uptake (adoption among the eligible)
  and adherence (SSaSS yr-5 ≈ 0.92) are assumptions; the whole-population coverage
  (s2) is a manual toggle. Household spillover is not modelled.
- **K→SBP evidence is sparser than Na→SBP, and additivity is assumed.** The
  potassium channel uses the Filippini (2020) achieved-excretion dose-response
  with unit-conversion assumptions (39.1 mg/mmol; intake→excretion ÷1.3) and a
  baseline-sodium modulation; the sodium- and potassium-mediated SBP changes are
  **assumed additive** (a factor lets this be relaxed). The K evidence base is
  thinner than for sodium.
- **LSS is benefit-only — no hyperkalaemia/CKD harm channel.** Unlike Huang et
  al., this disease model has no CKD state, so LSS benefits are **not offset** by
  potential renal harms. LSS effects should be read as upper-ish estimates in
  populations where hyperkalaemia risk matters.
- **Baseline potassium** is from Reddin 2023 with a **region-mean fallback** for
  countries absent from the source (Viet Nam → Southeast Asia; Ethiopia → Eastern
  Sub-Saharan Africa), so those two rest on regional, not national, data.
- **Na/K–SBP vs SSaSS applicability.** The two LSS methods are not
  interchangeable: SSaSS RRs apply only to SSaSS-comparable (diagnosed/treated
  HTN) populations and stroke outcomes, whereas Na/K–SBP covers all four causes
  via SBP. They are reported side by side, never combined, and no single pathway
  drives a cause twice.- **Euromonitor trend: category definitions, extrapolation, composition-only.**
  The packaged trend uses Matti's pre-combined v002 category set; the post-2030
  rule (`r RC$euromonitor$post2030`) and the ceiling
  (`r fmt_pct(RC$euromonitor$ceiling,0)`) are **extrapolation assumptions**, and
  the trend reweights *composition* only — total sodium intake is held fixed.
- **Fiscal policy is exploratory.** Pass-through, own-price elasticity, taxable
  share and substitution are uncertain and applying broad-category elasticities
  to high-sodium foods is contested; fiscal results are provisional, not
  confirmed. Its package membership follows `include_fiscal_in_package`.
- **Uncertainty not fully propagated.** Effect sizes, coverage, K→SBP anchors and
  the Euromonitor growth CI are largely used as point estimates; no probabilistic
  sensitivity analysis is run (the fiscal and Euromonitor CIs are shown but not
  propagated into deaths-delayed).
- **Source shares** for the ten prioritised countries are documented but several
  (notably Nigeria/Cameroon, with Nigeria a proxy for Cameroon) are provisional;
  any country outside the set falls back to the `default` (mean) profile. Public
  procurement uses a stale school-inclusive 5% share pending adults-only inputs.
- **Independent-cause structure.** The four causes share one population but are
  modelled independently, so "all-cause" prevalence/incidence sum cause-specific
  cases and may count comorbid individuals more than once.

# Deck artifacts (slide-deck export) {#deck-export}

This final section exists purely to hand computed elements to the Beamer slide
deck `docs/UWRTSL-sodium-policy.Rmd`. **All computation for the deck happens
here** (the deck itself performs none): every figure is written as a PNG and
every table/number is written into a single `deck_data.rds` bundle. The deck
loads that bundle and includes the PNGs, so the two documents can never drift.
Artifacts are written to `docs/deck_assets/`.

```{r deck-export, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE, results='hide'}
# ---- Output location --------------------------------------------------------
deck_dir <- file.path(wd, "docs", "deck_assets")
dir.create(deck_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

save_fig <- function(plot, name, w, h) {
  ggplot2::ggsave(filename = file.path(deck_dir, name), plot = plot,
                  width = w, height = h, units = "in", dpi = 300, bg = "white")
  invisible(name)
}

# Pre-render a data.frame to a booktabs LaTeX tabular, wrapped in \resizebox so
# it can never overflow a 16:9 Beamer frame. escape = TRUE handles %, & etc.
mk_tex <- function(df, align = NULL) {
  if (is.null(align)) align <- c("l", rep("r", ncol(df) - 1L))
  body <- knitr::kable(df, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, align = align,
                       linesep = "", escape = TRUE, row.names = FALSE)
  paste0("\\resizebox{\\textwidth}{!}{%\n", as.character(body), "\n}")
}

# ---- FIG: LSS Na/K causal pathway (deck Slide A) ----------------------------
mk_flow <- function(labels, fill = "#e8f2ea", border = "#59A14F") {
  n <- length(labels)
  bx <- data.table(x = seq_len(n), label = labels)
  ar <- data.table(x = (seq_len(n - 1)) + 0.44, xend = (2:n) - 0.44, y = 1, yend = 1)
  ggplot() +
    geom_tile(data = bx, aes(x = x, y = 1), width = 0.86, height = 0.7,
              fill = fill, color = border, linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_text(data = bx, aes(x = x, y = 1, label = label), size = 3.2, lineheight = 0.95) +
    geom_segment(data = ar, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend),
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.16, "cm"), type = "closed"),
                 linewidth = 0.5, color = "grey30") +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.5, n + 0.5), ylim = c(0.55, 1.45)) +
    theme_void(base_size = 12)
}

.s2_dk_names <- grep("^lss_s2_[0-9]+$", unique(as.data.table(lss_audit)$scenario), value = TRUE)
.s2_dk_rep   <- if (length(.s2_dk_names))
  .s2_dk_names[which.max(as.integer(sub("^lss_s2_", "", .s2_dk_names)))] else "lss_s2"
la_dk <- as.data.table(lss_audit)[scenario == .s2_dk_rep & method == "na_k_sbp"]

nums <- list(
  n_countries    = n_countries,
  study_years    = study_years,
  impact_window  = impact_window,
  scaleup1       = SCALEUP_YEAR1,
  scaleup2       = SCALEUP_YEAR2,
  horizon_end    = impact_y2,
  # headline deaths delayed (millions, formatted strings)
  pkg_m          = fmt_m(ddc("full_package"), 2),
  pkg_per_year_k = fmt_k(pkg_row$per_year, 0),
  pkg_pct        = fmt_pct(pkg_row$pct_vs_base, 1),
  salt_targets_m = fmt_m(ddc("salt_targets"), 2),

  lss_nacl         = fmt_pct(RC$lss$nacl_fraction, 0),
  lss_kcl          = fmt_pct(RC$lss$kcl_fraction, 0),
  lss_adherence    = formatC(RC$lss$adherence, format = "f", digits = 2),

  lss_harms        = RC$lss$harms_modelled,

  fiscal_taxable_share = fmt_pct(RC$fiscal$base$taxable_share, 0),
  fiscal_in_package    = as.character(RC$fiscal$include_in_package),

  fiscal_pass_through  = fmt_pct(fa_base$pass_through, 0),

  fiscal_price_change  = fmt_pct(fa_base$price_change, 0),
  fiscal_qty_response  = fmt_pct(abs(fa_base$quantity_response), 0),
  fiscal_taxed_pkg_red = fmt_pct(fa_base$taxed_packaged_reduction, 0),
  fiscal_pkg_red       = fmt_pct(fa_base$packaged_reduction, 1),
  fiscal_substitution  = fmt_pct(fa_base$substitution, 0),
  fiscal_reformulation = fmt_pct(fa_base$reformulation, 0),
  fiscal_low_pkg       = fmt_pct(fa_low$packaged_reduction, 1),
  fiscal_high_pkg      = fmt_pct(fa_high$packaged_reduction, 1),
  fiscal_low_m         = fmt_m(ddc("fiscal_low"), 2),
  fiscal_high_m        = fmt_m(ddc("fiscal_high"), 2),

  lss_uptake           = formatC(RC$lss$uptake, format = "f", digits = 2),

  lss_dsbp_na          = formatC(mean(la_dk$sbp_delta_na_mmHg,       na.rm = TRUE), format = "f", digits = 2),
  lss_dsbp_k           = formatC(mean(la_dk$sbp_delta_k_mmHg,        na.rm = TRUE), format = "f", digits = 2),

  lss_k_add            = formatC(mean(la_dk$potassium_added_g,       na.rm = TRUE), format = "f", digits = 2),
  # published media effect (retained in registry; excluded from reported scenarios)

  pkg_apc_range    = pkg_apc_range,
  # worked composition example: FOPL + salt targets on 'packaged'
  compose_fopl_salt = fmt_pct(1 - (1 - eff_of("fopl","packaged")) * (1 - eff_of("salt_targets","packaged")), 1),
  # SSaSS / LSS composition constants
  ssass_na_mgday   = "-350 mg/day",
  ssass_base_gday  = "4.3 g/day",
  ssass_sbp_mmhg   = "-3.34 mmHg",
  ssass_k_mgday    = "+803 mg/day",
  lss_ratio        = paste0(fmt_pct(RC$lss$nacl_fraction,0), " NaCl / ", fmt_pct(RC$lss$kcl_fraction,0), " KCl"),
  # benchmark vs the 100 Million Lives Saved 30% population sodium reduction
  bench_n          = length(sel_countries),
  bench_current_m  = if (benchmark_available) fmt_m(bench_cur_tot, 2)  else "n/a",
  bench_prev_m     = if (benchmark_available) fmt_m(bench_prev_tot, 2) else "n/a",
  bench_ratio      = if (benchmark_available)
                       formatC(bench_ratio_tot, format = "f", digits = 2) else "n/a"
)

# LaTeX-safe percent signs. The deck inlines these nums both in markdown text
# (where pandoc would escape a bare '%') AND inside raw-LaTeX environments
# (tabular / itemize / block) where it would NOT -- an unescaped '%' there
# becomes a comment and silently eats the rest of the line. Pre-escaping every
# '%' to '\%' is correct in both contexts, so it is done once here.
nums <- lapply(nums, function(v)
  if (is.character(v)) gsub("%", "\\\\%", v, perl = TRUE) else v)

# ---- NEW deck artifacts (Task 4i): year-specific shares, LSS Na/K pathway, ---
# NCD-RisC eligibility, Na/K-vs-SSaSS, fiscal audit. Guarded so a skipped chunk
# never breaks the bundle.
if (exists("fig_pkg_time")) save_fig(fig_pkg_time, "fig_packaged_time.png", 10, 5)
tex_ncd_eligibility <- if (exists("he_tbl")) mk_tex(as.data.frame(he_tbl),
  align = c("l","l", rep("r",6))) else "\\emph{NCD-RisC eligibility unavailable.}"
tex_lss_audit <- if (exists("la_tbl")) mk_tex(as.data.frame(la_tbl),
  align = c("l","l", rep("r",8))) else "\\emph{LSS audit unavailable.}"
tex_fiscal_audit <- if (exists("fa_tbl")) mk_tex(as.data.frame(fa_tbl),
  align = c("l", rep("r",10))) else "\\emph{Fiscal audit unavailable.}"
tex_nak_ssass <- if (exists("cmp_tbl")) mk_tex(as.data.frame(cmp_tbl),
  align = c("l","l","l", rep("r",5))) else "\\emph{Na/K-vs-SSaSS comparison unavailable.}"
tex_fiscal_sensitivity <- if (exists("fr_tbl")) mk_tex(as.data.frame(fr_tbl),
  align = c("l","r","r")) else "\\emph{Fiscal sensitivity results unavailable.}"
tex_huang_ours  <- if (exists("huang_cmp"))  mk_tex(huang_cmp,  align = c("l","l","l")) else "\\emph{Huang comparison unavailable.}"
tex_saxena_ours <- if (exists("saxena_cmp")) mk_tex(saxena_cmp, align = c("l","l","l")) else "\\emph{Saxena comparison unavailable.}"

figs <- list(
  source_shares = "fig_source_shares.png",
  salteff       = "fig_salteff.png",
  salteff_pkg   = "fig_salteff_pkg.png",
  flow          = "fig_flow.png",

)

saveRDS(deck, file = file.path(deck_dir, "deck_data.rds"))
```

# Technical report artifacts (Word + Excel export) {#tr-artifacts}

This closing section is the **authoritative producer** of the Word technical report and the Excel workbook. It consumes the model outputs and objects computed above, builds every technical-report table and figure, and writes a single artifact bundle (`docs/report_assets/tr_bundle.rds`) plus `docs/technical-report.xlsx`. `docs/technical-report.RMD` only lays these out; it performs no calculation.

```{r tr-setup-tables, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}
# ============================================================================
# TECHNICAL-REPORT ARTIFACTS  (authoritative producer for docs/technical-report.*)
# Builds every number, table and figure the Word technical report needs, writes a
# single artifact bundle (docs/report_assets/tr_bundle.rds) AND the Excel workbook
# (docs/technical-report.xlsx). docs/technical-report.RMD only LAYS OUT these.
# ============================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- tr-setup ----
library(openxlsx)
ra_dir <- file.path(wd, "docs", "report_assets")
dir.create(ra_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# ---- RTSL brand palette (single source of truth for the technical report) ----
# Hex values are taken from Resolve to Save Lives' OFFICIAL sources, not inferred:
#   * the live site's named `--rtsl-*` CSS custom properties (resolvetosavelives.org
#     and .../how-we-save-lives/healthier-food/);
#   * the "6-Step Sodium Reduction Guide" fact sheet (heading/number colour #382986,
#     alert icon #e83740);
#   * the "Research Prioritization ... Low-Sodium Salt Substitutes" report.
# Roles below mirror RTSL's own usage (purple = primary/brand & headings; orange =
# secondary/accent; red = alert; a named neutral "chart grey" for baseline series).
RTSL <- list(
  purple    = "#382986",  # --rtsl-purple: primary brand / headings / table header
  orange    = "#F3775C",  # --rtsl-orange: secondary / accent
  red       = "#E8383D",  # --rtsl-red: emphasis / alert
  lpurple1  = "#6577BA",  # --rtsl-light-purple-1: secondary graphic / mono charts
  lpurple2  = "#B2B1D9",  # --rtsl-light-purple-2: mid tint
  lpurple3  = "#E6E8F5",  # --rtsl-light-purple-3: pale fills / icon backgrounds
  lpurple4  = "#F5F6FC",  # --rtsl-light-purple-4: near-white lavender (row banding)
  dgreen    = "#40BD52",  # --rtsl-dark-green: positive / achieved
  lgreen    = "#85BD40",  # --rtsl-light-green
  yellow    = "#FCBA24",  # --rtsl-yellow: callout
  gold      = "#F79736",  # gradient gold companion to the yellow
  text      = "#25252C",  # --rtsl-text / --rtsl-soft-black: body text
  midgrey   = "#69697D",  # --rtsl-mid-grey: muted text
  divider   = "#B4B6C5",  # --rtsl-divider: hairlines / gridlines
  chartgrey = "#E4E7EE",  # --rtsl-chart-grey: NEUTRAL baseline / reference fill
  white     = "#FFFFFF"
)

# Table/figure styling pushed into the bundle so the consumer only RENDERS it.
TR_STYLE <- list(header_bg = RTSL$purple, header_fg = RTSL$white,
                 band = RTSL$lpurple4, rule = RTSL$divider, text = RTSL$text,
                 baseline = RTSL$chartgrey)

# Semantic colour maps reused across every technical-report figure. Same source /
# same intervention family -> same colour everywhere. Inherent sodium (never
# targeted) and any baseline/reference series take the neutral chart grey.
rtsl_source_cols <- c(discretionary = RTSL$purple, packaged = RTSL$orange,
  restaurant = RTSL$lpurple1, public = RTSL$dgreen, inherent = RTSL$chartgrey)
# Intervention family -> colour. Full package is the hero (purple); LSS is the
# green "opportunity" family; packaged-food levers share the accent orange.
rtsl_scn_family <- function(scn) data.table::fifelse(scn == "baseline", "baseline",
  data.table::fifelse(grepl("full_package", scn), "package",
  data.table::fifelse(grepl("^lss", scn), "lss",
  data.table::fifelse(grepl("fiscal", scn), "fiscal",
  data.table::fifelse(scn %in% c("salt_targets", "fopl"), "packaged",
  data.table::fifelse(scn == "public_procurement", "procurement", "other"))))))
rtsl_scn_cols <- function(scns) {
  fam <- rtsl_scn_family(scns)
  pal <- c(baseline = RTSL$chartgrey, package = RTSL$purple, lss = RTSL$dgreen,
           fiscal = RTSL$lpurple1, packaged = RTSL$orange,
           procurement = RTSL$lgreen, other = RTSL$midgrey)
  setNames(unname(pal[fam]), scns)
}

# Clean, restrained theme: RTSL body-text colour, muted horizontal gridlines only,
# no chart-junk. Figure TITLES are rendered above the image by the report from the
# bundle, so figures carry NO embedded plot title/subtitle.
tr_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(text = element_text(colour = RTSL$text),
        axis.text = element_text(colour = RTSL$text),
        axis.title = element_text(colour = RTSL$text, size = 10),
        plot.title = element_blank(), plot.subtitle = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = RTSL$divider, linewidth = 0.3),
        legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_text(size = 9),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 9))

save_tr_fig <- function(plot, file, w, h, dpi = 300) {
  fp <- file.path(ra_dir, file)
  ggplot2::ggsave(fp, plot = plot, width = w, height = h, units = "in",
                  dpi = dpi, bg = "white")
  fp
}

# Deaths delayed by country x scenario over the impact window (authoritative key).
dd_cs  <- deaths_delayed_by(data.out, by = "location", years = impact_y1:impact_y2)
dd_cs[, scenario := as.character(scenario)]
ddw    <- dcast(dd_cs, location ~ scenario, value.var = "deaths_delayed")
base_cs <- unique(dd_cs[, .(location, baseline_dead)])

# Country display order: by full-package (base) deaths delayed, descending.
country_order <- ddw[order(-full_package), location]
n_pri <- length(country_order)

# Deaths delayed by country x scenario x cause (for supplemental by-cause table).
dd_csc <- deaths_delayed_by(data.out, by = c("location", "cause"),
                            years = impact_y1:impact_y2)
dd_csc[, scenario := as.character(scenario)]

# Build a display+raw deaths-delayed table (thousands, 1 dp) with a Total row.
mk_dd_table <- function(scen_cols, col_labels, total_lab = "Total") {
  present <- scen_cols %in% names(ddw)
  scen_cols <- scen_cols[present]; col_labels <- col_labels[present]
  m <- ddw[match(country_order, location), c("location", scen_cols), with = FALSE]
  tot <- cbind(data.table(location = total_lab),
               m[, lapply(.SD, sum, na.rm = TRUE), .SDcols = scen_cols])
  m2 <- rbind(m, tot, use.names = TRUE)
  raw <- copy(m2); setnames(raw, c("location", scen_cols), c("Country", col_labels))
  disp <- copy(m2)
  for (s in scen_cols)
    disp[[s]] <- formatC(disp[[s]] / 1e3, format = "f", digits = 1, big.mark = ",")
  setnames(disp, c("location", scen_cols), c("Country", col_labels))
  list(display = as.data.frame(disp), raw = as.data.frame(raw),
       scen = scen_cols, labels = col_labels)
}

fmtm <- function(x, d = 2) formatC(x / 1e6, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")
fmtk <- function(x, d = 0) formatC(x / 1e3, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")
pct  <- function(x, d = 1) paste0(formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = d), "%")
# Plain-language rendering of the post-2030 packaged-trend rule (no code tokens).
.euro_post2030 <- switch(as.character(RC$euromonitor$post2030),
  hold_constant = "held constant", continue_trend = "trend continues",
  converge_to_ceiling = "converges to ceiling", as.character(RC$euromonitor$post2030))

# Replace any implementation-style intervention token that may appear inside a
# scenario label (e.g. the base full-package label lists "public_procurement +
# fopl + salt_targets + fiscal") with plain language, longest keys first.
.friendly_iv <- c(public_procurement = "public food procurement", fopl = "front-of-pack labelling",
  salt_targets = "salt targets", fiscal_low = "salt tax (low)", fiscal_base = "salt tax (base)",
  fiscal_high = "salt tax (high)", fiscal = "salt tax",
  lss = "low-sodium salt substitute")
clean_label <- function(s) {
  s <- as.character(s)
  for (k in names(.friendly_iv)[order(-nchar(names(.friendly_iv)))])
    s <- gsub(k, .friendly_iv[[k]], s, fixed = TRUE)
  # (Comment 8) The fiscal status is defined once near the top of the report; strip the
  # "EXPLORATORY" label that the scenario registry bakes into fiscal scenario names.
  s <- gsub("\\s*\\(EXPLORATORY salt tax\\)", " (salt tax)", s, ignore.case = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("EXPLORATORY[- ]?", "", s, ignore.case = TRUE)
  # (Comment 1) Replace an em dash used as a label separator (e.g. "Full package — low
  # salt tax variant") with a colon so no em dash reaches the Word report.
  s <- gsub("\\s*\u2014\\s*", ": ", s)
  trimws(gsub("\\s+", " ", s))
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------- tr-tables ----
# Registries collect table/figure metadata; NUMBERS are assigned by Word-appearance
# order (TABLE_ORDER / FIGURE_ORDER) so bundle == workbook == Word identifiers.
TAB <- list(); FIG <- list()
# (Comment 1) Safety net: remove em dashes from any DISPLAY cell (some reused upstream
# tables carry them), replacing a between-words em dash with a comma, a whole-cell em
# dash with "n/a", and any remainder with an en dash.
.de_emdash <- function(df) {
  fx <- function(z) { z <- gsub("^\\s*\u2014\\s*$", "n/a", z)
    z <- gsub("\\s+\u2014\\s+", ", ", z); gsub("\u2014", "\u2013", z) }
  df[] <- lapply(df, function(col) if (is.character(col) || is.factor(col)) fx(as.character(col)) else col)
  df
}
add_tab <- function(key, title, display, raw = NULL, units = "", period = "",
                    population = "", scenario_def = "", rounding = "", source = "",
                    notes = "", fontsize = 9, orientation = "portrait") {
  display <- .de_emdash(as.data.frame(display, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
  TAB[[key]] <<- list(key = key, title = title, display = display,
    raw = if (is.null(raw)) display else raw, units = units, period = period,
    population = population, scenario_def = scenario_def, rounding = rounding,
    source = source, notes = notes, fontsize = fontsize, orientation = orientation)
}
add_fig <- function(key, title, file, w, h, notes = "", data = NULL, source = "",
                    units = "", period = "", population = "") {
  FIG[[key]] <<- list(key = key, title = title, file = file, w = w, h = h,
                      notes = notes, data = data, source = source,
                      units = units, period = period, population = population)
}

WINDOW <- impact_window
POP_ADULT <- "Adults aged 20 to 95"

# Standardized visible producer/source line for every table and figure (comment 6).
# Upstream data provenance stays in the notes/methods/evidence, not on this line.
REPORT_SOURCE <- "UW/RTSL sodium policy model"

# T: Countries & populations -------------------------------------------------
SBP_BASE_YEAR <- 2026L   # baseline / reference year for the reported population & SBP
pop_base <- data.out[cause == "ihd" & year == SBP_BASE_YEAR & scenario == "baseline",
                     .(pop = sum(pop, na.rm = TRUE)), by = location]
sodium_ct <- tryCatch({
  sp <- readRDS(paste0(wd_data, "sodium_policy_scenarios.rds")); setDT(sp)
  sp[year == 2024, .(location, sodium_current)]
}, error = function(e) NULL)
cp <- data.table(location = country_order)
cp <- merge(cp, pop_base, by = "location", all.x = TRUE)
if (!is.null(sodium_ct)) cp <- merge(cp, sodium_ct, by = "location", all.x = TRUE)

# ---- Comment A: baseline mean SBP, population-weighted, stated as 2026 --------
# Uses the SAME authoritative NCD-RisC age-sex blood-pressure distribution that
# feeds the model (bp_data6.csv -> data.in): mean SBP and raised-BP fraction by
# 5-year age group and sex, held at the modelled baseline distribution. It is
# aggregated to the country level by weighting each age-sex cell by that country's
# modelled adult population in SBP_BASE_YEAR (NOT an unweighted mean over age/sex).
pop_wts <- data.out[cause == "ihd" & scenario == "baseline" & year == SBP_BASE_YEAR,
                    .(popw = sum(pop, na.rm = TRUE)), by = .(location, sex, age)]
bp_raw <- tryCatch({ b <- fread(paste0(wd_data, "bp_data6.csv")); setDT(b); b },
                   error = function(e) NULL)
if (is.null(bp_raw) || !nrow(pop_wts))
  stop("Comment A (baseline SBP): the authoritative NCD-RisC age-sex blood-pressure ",
       "data (bp_data6.csv -> data.in) and/or the ", SBP_BASE_YEAR,
       " modelled adult population are not available to report.RMD; ",
       "refusing to invent baseline SBP values.")
# Map each single year of age to its NCD-RisC 5-year group (85 = terminal 85+).
pop_wts[, agrp := pmin(5L * (age %/% 5L), 85L)]
bp_grp <- bp_raw[, .(location = Country, sex, agrp = age, Mean, raisedBP)]
sbp_join <- merge(pop_wts, bp_grp, by = c("location", "sex", "agrp"), all.x = TRUE)
if (anyNA(sbp_join[location %in% country_order, Mean]))
  stop("Comment A (baseline SBP): unmatched age-sex cells joining the NCD-RisC BP ",
       "distribution to the ", SBP_BASE_YEAR, " population; refusing to invent values.")
bp_src <- sbp_join[, .(sbp = sum(Mean * popw) / sum(popw),
                       raised = sum(raisedBP * popw) / sum(popw)), by = location]
cp <- merge(cp, bp_src, by = "location", all.x = TRUE)

# ---- Comment 3: NCD-RisC (2021) hypertension prevalence, all-sex --------------
# Uses htn_eligibility$htn_prev (the age-standardised 30-79 estimate that also sizes
# the NCD-RisC eligibility table), combined to one all-sex country value by weighting
# the male/female estimates with the 2026 modelled population aged 30-79 by sex.
# This is a DIFFERENT measure from the raised-BP fraction in the BP-distribution file.
htn_e <- as.data.table(htn_eligibility)[, .(location, sex, htn_prev)]
pop_3079 <- data.out[cause == "ihd" & scenario == "baseline" & year == SBP_BASE_YEAR &
                     age >= 30 & age <= 79, .(popw = sum(pop, na.rm = TRUE)),
                     by = .(location, sex)]
htn_j <- merge(pop_3079, htn_e, by = c("location", "sex"), all.x = TRUE)
if (anyNA(htn_j[location %in% country_order, htn_prev]) || !nrow(pop_3079))
  stop("Comment 3 (hypertension prevalence): NCD-RisC htn_eligibility$htn_prev or the ",
       SBP_BASE_YEAR, " sex-specific 30-79 population is unavailable; refusing to invent values.")
htn_src <- htn_j[, .(htn_prev = sum(htn_prev * popw) / sum(popw)), by = location]
cp <- merge(cp, htn_src, by = "location", all.x = TRUE)

cp <- cp[match(country_order, location)]
cp_disp <- data.frame(
  Country = cp$location,
  `Adult population, 2026 (millions)` = formatC(cp$pop / 1e6, format = "f", digits = 1, big.mark = ","),
  `Baseline sodium, 2024 (g/day)` = if (!is.null(sodium_ct)) formatC(cp$sodium_current, format = "f", digits = 2) else "n/a",
  `Mean SBP, 2026 (mmHg)` = formatC(cp$sbp, format = "f", digits = 0),
  `Raised BP, 2026 (%)` = pct(cp$raised, 0),
  `Hypertension, NCD-RisC 2021 (%)` = pct(cp$htn_prev, 0),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
add_tab("countries", "Countries and populations included, with baseline blood pressure", cp_disp,
  units = "Population in millions; sodium in g/day; SBP in mmHg; prevalences as % of adults",
  period = "Population and blood pressure 2026; sodium 2024",
  population = POP_ADULT,
  source = REPORT_SOURCE,
  notes = paste0("Adult population is the ", SBP_BASE_YEAR, " baseline-scenario population aged 20 to 95 ",
    "(UN World Population Prospects 2024); baseline sodium is the 2024 country mean (GBD/Marklund). ",
    "Mean SBP and Raised BP are the NCD-RisC age-sex blood-pressure distribution that feeds the model, ",
    "population-weighted by each country's ", SBP_BASE_YEAR, " modelled adult population (not an ",
    "unweighted mean over age or sex). Raised BP is the NCD-RisC raised-blood-pressure fraction; ",
    "Hypertension is the distinct NCD-RisC (2021) age-standardised 30-79 hypertension prevalence, ",
    "combined across sexes by 2026 population weight. Nigeria's profile is applied to Cameroon ",
    "because a country-specific profile was unavailable."),
  orientation = "landscape", fontsize = 8)

# T: Intervention effect-size summary (BRIEF, body) --------------------------
eff_of <- function(iv, src) { v <- intervention_effects[intervention == iv & source == src, effect]
  if (length(v) == 0) NA_real_ else v[1] }
# Comment 7: the body effect-size table now MERGES the former appendix evidence table
# (interventions + the two shared pathway rows + concise evidence citations).
brief_eff <- data.frame(
  Intervention = c("Public food procurement", "Salt targets (reformulation)",
                   "Front-of-pack labelling", "Fiscal policy (salt tax)",
                   "Low-sodium salt substitutes (Scenarios 2/4/5)",
                   "Sodium to blood pressure", "Blood pressure to cardiovascular disease"),
  `Sodium source targeted` = c("Public/institutional food", "Packaged food",
                   "Packaged food", "Packaged food", "Discretionary salt",
                   "All sodium sources", "n/a"),
  `Modelled effect` = c(
     pct(eff_of("public_procurement", "public"), 0),
     pct(eff_of("salt_targets", "packaged"), 0),
     pct(eff_of("fopl", "packaged"), 1),
     paste0(pct(RC$fiscal$base_effect, 0), " of packaged (base)"),
     paste0(pct(RC$lss$eff_lss_na_k_discretionary, 0), " of discretionary Na + K gain"),
     "2.8 mmHg/g raised BP; 1.0 mmHg/g normal BP",
     "Relative risk per 10 mmHg SBP, by cause"),
  `Blood-pressure or health pathway` = c(
     rep("Lower sodium lowers SBP", 4),
     "Lower sodium and higher potassium lower SBP",
     "SBP dose-response to sodium (and potassium)",
     "Lower SBP lowers incidence of the four causes"),
  `Evidence source` = c(
     "Gase et al. (2011)", "He et al. (2013)", "Taillie et al. (2024)",
     "Saxena et al. (2025); Cobiac et al. (2017)",
     "Huang et al. (2026); Neal et al. (2021); Filippini et al. (2020); Reddin et al. (2023)",
     "Filippini et al. (2020, 2021)", "Ettehad et al. (2016); GBD 2019"),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
add_tab("eff_brief", "Modelled interventions, effect sizes and evidence", brief_eff,
  units = "Relative reduction of the targeted sodium source at full implementation, unless noted",
  period = paste0("Scale-up ", SCALEUP_YEAR1, "–", SCALEUP_YEAR2),
  source = REPORT_SOURCE,
  notes = paste0("Each policy is applied only to the sodium sources it can reach. Modelled ",
    "values follow the production configuration and may differ from a single published study ",
    "(for example, salt targets are modelled at 20% against about 15% observed in the United ",
    "Kingdom over nine years). The salt-substitute effect combines a discretionary-sodium ",
    "displacement with a potassium gain, so its full health effect is not a single percentage. ",
    "The final two rows give the shared sodium and potassium to blood-pressure to disease pathway."),
  fontsize = 8, orientation = "landscape")

# T: MAIN country x intervention (client Table 1) ----------------------------
main_scen <- c("public_procurement", "salt_targets", "fopl",
               "fiscal_low", "fiscal_base", "fiscal_high",
               "full_package_low", "full_package", "full_package_high")
main_lab  <- c("Public food procurement", "Salt targets", "Front-of-pack labelling",
               "Fiscal: low", "Fiscal: base", "Fiscal: high",
               "Package total (low fiscal)", "Package total (base fiscal)",
               "Package total (high fiscal)")
T_main <- mk_dd_table(main_scen, main_lab, total_lab = paste0("Total (", n_pri, " countries)"))
add_tab("main", "Deaths delayed by country and intervention: packaged-food and public-procurement policies",
  T_main$display, T_main$raw,
  units = "Thousands of cardiovascular deaths delayed vs. baseline",
  period = WINDOW, population = POP_ADULT,
  scenario_def = "Each column is an independent model run. Package totals are joint runs of public procurement + salt targets + FOPL + fiscal (at the low/base/high fiscal variant); they are NOT the sum of the individual policy columns.",
  rounding = "Nearest 100 deaths (0.1 thousand). Total row = sum of country rows per column.",
  source = REPORT_SOURCE,
  notes = "Public food procurement is modelled using an assumed 5% institutional share of sodium.",
  fontsize = 8, orientation = "landscape")

# T: LSS uptake (client Table 2) ---------------------------------------------
s2_reg <- as.data.table(RC$scenarios)[grepl("^lss_s2_[0-9]+$", scenario)]
s2_reg[, cov := as.numeric(lss_coverage)]; setorder(s2_reg, cov)
lss_scen <- c(s2_reg$scenario, "lss_s4", "lss_s5")
lss_lab  <- c(paste0("Scenario 2: ", round(100 * s2_reg$cov), "% uptake"),
              "Scenario 4: diagnosed HTN", "Scenario 5: treated HTN")
T_lss <- mk_dd_table(lss_scen, lss_lab, total_lab = paste0("Total (", n_pri, " countries)"))
add_tab("lss", "Deaths delayed by country: discretionary-sodium replacement with low-sodium salt substitutes",
  T_lss$display, T_lss$raw,
  units = "Thousands of cardiovascular deaths delayed vs. baseline",
  period = WINDOW, population = POP_ADULT,
  scenario_def = "Scenario 2 = whole-population LSS at the stated population uptake. Scenario 4 = adults with diagnosed hypertension. Scenario 5 = adults with treated hypertension (NCD-RisC eligibility).",
  rounding = "Nearest 100 deaths (0.1 thousand). Total row = sum of country rows per column.",
  source = REPORT_SOURCE,
  notes = "Mechanistic sodium-and-potassium blood-pressure method (benefit-only; no hyperkalaemia/CKD harms). Uptake is population reach, distinct from adherence and the KCl substitution fraction.",
  fontsize = 8, orientation = "landscape")

# T: Deaths delayed by scenario (all-cause summary) --------------------------
scn_sum_order <- c("public_procurement", "fopl", "salt_targets",
                   "fiscal_low", "fiscal_base", "fiscal_high",
                   s2_reg$scenario, "lss_s4", "lss_s5", "lss_s4_ssass", "lss_s5_ssass",
                   "full_package_low", "full_package", "full_package_high")
scn_sum_order <- scn_sum_order[scn_sum_order %in% as.character(dd_cum$scenario)]
ss <- dd_cum[match(scn_sum_order, as.character(scenario))]
scn_sum <- data.frame(
  Scenario = clean_label(scenario_labels[as.character(ss$scenario)]),
  `Deaths delayed (thousands)` = formatC(ss$deaths_delayed / 1e3, format = "f", digits = 1, big.mark = ","),
  `Average per year (thousands)` = formatC(ss$per_year / 1e3, format = "f", digits = 1, big.mark = ","),
  `% of baseline CVD deaths` = pct(ss$pct_vs_base, 2),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
scn_sum_raw <- data.frame(Scenario = clean_label(scenario_labels[as.character(ss$scenario)]),
  deaths_delayed = ss$deaths_delayed, per_year = ss$per_year,
  pct_of_baseline = 100 * ss$pct_vs_base, check.names = FALSE)
add_tab("scn_summary", "Cumulative deaths delayed by scenario (all countries, all causes)",
  scn_sum, scn_sum_raw,
  units = "Thousands of deaths delayed; percent of baseline CVD deaths in the window",
  period = WINDOW, population = POP_ADULT,
  rounding = "Nearest 100 deaths (0.1 thousand).",
  source = REPORT_SOURCE,
  notes = "LSS scenarios are separate from the package. SSaSS trial-RR rows are a stroke-only benchmark.")

# T: Full package by cause ---------------------------------------------------
dd_cause_pkg <- deaths_delayed_by(data.out, by = "cause", years = impact_y1:impact_y2)
dd_cause_pkg <- dd_cause_pkg[as.character(scenario) == "full_package"]
setorder(dd_cause_pkg, -deaths_delayed)
bycause <- data.frame(
  Cause = cause_map[dd_cause_pkg$cause],
  `Deaths delayed (thousands)` = formatC(dd_cause_pkg$deaths_delayed / 1e3, format = "f", digits = 1, big.mark = ","),
  `Share of package total` = pct(dd_cause_pkg$deaths_delayed / sum(dd_cause_pkg$deaths_delayed), 1),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
bycause_raw <- data.frame(Cause = cause_map[dd_cause_pkg$cause],
  deaths_delayed = dd_cause_pkg$deaths_delayed,
  share = dd_cause_pkg$deaths_delayed / sum(dd_cause_pkg$deaths_delayed), check.names = FALSE)
add_tab("bycause", "Full package: deaths delayed by cardiovascular cause",
  bycause, bycause_raw,
  units = "Thousands of deaths delayed; share of package total",
  period = WINDOW, population = POP_ADULT,
  scenario_def = "Full package at base fiscal.",
  rounding = "Nearest 100 deaths.",
  source = REPORT_SOURCE)

# T: Limitations / assumptions -----------------------------------------------
lim <- data.frame(
  Area = c("Outcome metric", "LSS harms", "Fiscal policy", "Public procurement share",
           "Hypertension eligibility", "Baseline potassium", "Packaged-food trend",
           "Sodium-source data", "Uncertainty"),
  `Assumption / limitation` = c(
    "Sodium-to-SBP policies lower incidence, not case fatality, so deaths are DELAYED (shifted later), not permanently averted; totals depend on the accounting window.",
    "LSS is modelled benefit-only: this disease model has no chronic-kidney-disease / hyperkalaemia state, so potential renal harms are not offset.",
    "The salt-tax pathway depends on pass-through, price elasticity, taxable share and substitution, which are uncertain, and broad-category elasticities may not transfer to high-sodium foods.",
    "Public food procurement is modelled using an assumed 5% institutional share of sodium.",
    "Diagnosed/treated hypertension shares (Scenarios 4/5) are age-standardised 30–79 values applied across all ages and held constant after the source year.",
    "Potassium intake for Viet Nam and Ethiopia uses a regional mean rather than national data.",
    "The packaged-food share follows a country-specific growth trend with an 80% ceiling and a post-2030 hold; these are extrapolation assumptions. The other source shares are rescaled to keep the five summing to 100%, so total baseline sodium intake does not grow; only its composition changes.",
    "Country source shares are documented, and where a country-specific profile was unavailable (notably Cameroon) a proxy or default profile is used.",
    "Effect sizes, coverage and dose-response anchors are treated as point estimates; results do not include full probabilistic uncertainty."),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
add_tab("limitations", "Key assumptions and limitations", lim,
  source = REPORT_SOURCE,
  notes = "Assumptions and limitations that bear on interpretation of the results.")

cat("tr-tables: built", length(TAB), "core tables so far.\n")
```

```{r tr-appendix-tables, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}
# ------------------------------------------------ tr-tables-appendix ----
# APPENDIX tables. Where report.RMD already built a clean, display-ready object
# (he_tbl, bk_tbl, la_tbl, cmp_tbl, fa_tbl, pkg_trend_tbl, huang_cmp, saxena_cmp,
# bt_fmt) we REUSE it so the Word doc and HTML report can never diverge.

# Friendly-name map so no implementation-style identifiers reach the Word report.
friendly_iv <- c(public_procurement = "public food procurement",
  fopl = "front-of-pack labelling", salt_targets = "salt targets",
  fiscal = "salt tax", fiscal_low = "salt tax (low)", fiscal_base = "salt tax (base)",
  fiscal_high = "salt tax (high)",
  lss = "low-sodium salt substitute")
friendly_ivs <- function(s) {
  if (is.na(s) || s == "") return("None (baseline)")
  parts <- trimws(strsplit(s, "\\+")[[1]])
  paste(ifelse(parts %in% names(friendly_iv), friendly_iv[parts], parts), collapse = " + ")
}

# T: Scenario definitions ----------------------------------------------------
scn_reg2 <- as.data.table(RC$scenarios)
scn_def <- data.frame(
  Scenario = clean_label(scn_reg2$label),
  `Constituent interventions` = vapply(scn_reg2$interventions, friendly_ivs, character(1)),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
add_tab("scn_def", "Full scenario definitions", scn_def,
  source = REPORT_SOURCE,
  notes = "The five Scenario-2 rows are the whole-population low-sodium-salt uptake sweep. SSaSS rows are a stroke-only benchmark. Package rows differ only in the salt-tax variant.")

# (Comment 7) The former appendix "Intervention effect sizes and evidence sources"
# table (eff_evidence) has been MERGED into the body table eff_brief and removed.

# T: Sodium-source assumptions by country ------------------------------------
ss_raw <- copy(source_shares)[location != "default"][match(country_order, location)]
ss_appx_disp <- data.frame(
  Country = ss_raw$location,
  Discretionary = pct(ss_raw$discretionary, 1), Packaged = pct(ss_raw$packaged, 1),
  Restaurant = pct(ss_raw$restaurant, 1), `Public/institutional` = pct(ss_raw$public, 1),
  Inherent = pct(ss_raw$inherent, 1), check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
ss_appx_raw <- data.frame(Country = ss_raw$location,
  Discretionary = ss_raw$discretionary, Packaged = ss_raw$packaged,
  Restaurant = ss_raw$restaurant, Public = ss_raw$public, Inherent = ss_raw$inherent,
  check.names = FALSE)
add_tab("source_shares", "Sodium source shares by country (base year)", ss_appx_disp, ss_appx_raw,
  units = "Fraction of total baseline sodium intake", period = paste0("Base year ", RC$euromonitor$base_year),
  source = REPORT_SOURCE,
  notes = paste0("Source shares are from the RTSL sodium policy document. Rows sum to 100%. ",
    "Inherent sodium is never targeted. Nigeria's profile is applied to Cameroon because a ",
    "country-specific profile was unavailable; a country without its own profile uses a default ",
    "average. Shares become year-specific via the packaged-food trend."))

# T: NCD-RisC eligibility (reuse he_tbl) -------------------------------------
if (exists("he_tbl")) add_tab("ncd_elig", "Hypertension eligibility by country and sex (Scenarios 4 and 5)",
  as.data.frame(he_tbl),
  units = "Age-standardised proportions (30–79)", period = paste0("Source year ", RC$htn_source_year),
  source = REPORT_SOURCE,
  notes = "Diagnosed/treated hypertension shares are from the NCD Risk Factor Collaboration (2021); they size LSS Scenarios 4 and 5.", fontsize = 8)

# T: Baseline potassium (reuse bk_tbl) ---------------------------------------
if (exists("bk_tbl")) add_tab("baseline_k", "Baseline potassium intake by country and sex",
  as.data.frame(bk_tbl), units = "g/day",
  source = REPORT_SOURCE,
  notes = "Baseline potassium intake is from a global pooled analysis (Reddin et al., 2023); Viet Nam and Ethiopia use a regional mean rather than national data.")

# T: LSS Na/K audit (reuse la_tbl) -------------------------------------------
if (exists("la_tbl")) add_tab("lss_audit", "Low-sodium salt substitute pathway quantities (Scenario 2, representative coverage)",
  as.data.frame(la_tbl),
  units = "Sodium/potassium in g/day; SBP change in mmHg",
  source = REPORT_SOURCE,
  notes = "Composition scales linearly with coverage; harms not modelled.", fontsize = 8, orientation = "landscape")

# T: Na/K vs SSaSS (reuse cmp_tbl; strip implementation-style tokens) --------
if (exists("cmp_tbl")) {
  cmp_clean <- as.data.frame(cmp_tbl)
  if ("Method" %in% names(cmp_clean))
    cmp_clean$Method <- c(na_k_sbp = "Sodium/potassium → SBP (mechanistic)",
      ssass_trial_rr = "SSaSS trial benchmark")[cmp_clean$Method]
  if ("Eligibility" %in% names(cmp_clean))
    cmp_clean$Eligibility <- c(whole_population = "Whole population",
      diagnosed_pop = "Diagnosed hypertension", treated_pop = "Treated hypertension")[cmp_clean$Eligibility]
  add_tab("nak_ssass", "Low-sodium salt substitutes: mechanistic sodium/potassium vs. SSaSS trial benchmark",
    cmp_clean,
    units = "Exposure change in g/day; SBP in mmHg; deaths delayed in millions",
    period = WINDOW, source = REPORT_SOURCE,
    notes = "Distinct pathways (all-CVD via blood pressure vs. stroke-only relative risk); shown side by side, never combined. Trial relative risks are from the SSaSS trial (Neal et al., 2021).", fontsize = 8, orientation = "landscape")
}

# T: Fiscal pathway (reuse fa_tbl; friendly variant names) -------------------
if (exists("fa_tbl")) {
  fa_clean <- as.data.frame(fa_tbl)
  if ("Variant" %in% names(fa_clean))
    fa_clean$Variant <- c(fiscal_low = "Low", fiscal_base = "Base",
      fiscal_high = "High", fiscal = "Base")[fa_clean$Variant]
  add_tab("fiscal_path", "Salt-tax pathway by sensitivity variant",
    fa_clean,
    units = "Percentages except elasticity", source = REPORT_SOURCE,
    notes = "Pathway parameters follow Saxena et al. (2025). 'Δ total packaged' = Δ taxed packaged × taxable share.", fontsize = 7, orientation = "landscape")
}

# T: Packaged-food trend (reuse pkg_trend_tbl) -------------------------------
if (exists("pkg_trend_tbl") && !is.null(pkg_trend_tbl)) add_tab("pkg_trend", "Packaged-food sodium-share growth by country",
  as.data.frame(pkg_trend_tbl),
  units = "Annual percent change; packaged share in percent",
  source = REPORT_SOURCE,
  notes = paste0("Packaged-food growth trend from commercial sales data (Euromonitor, Marklund). ",
    "Applied as (1+g)^(year-base) to the packaged share, capped at ",
    pct(RC$euromonitor$ceiling, 0), "; other sources renormalise; composition-only."))

# T: Key model inputs & parameters -------------------------------------------
key_inputs <- data.frame(
  Parameter = c("Countries modelled", "Initialization year", "Epidemiologic seed year",
    "Scale-up window",
    "Projection horizon", "Results years", "Cardiovascular causes", "Sodium sources",
    "Sodium-to-SBP slope (raised BP / normal BP)", "Minimum sodium floor",
    "LSS composition (NaCl / KCl)", "LSS adherence", "LSS uptake among reached",
    "K added per g Na displaced", "K unit conversion (mg/mmol; intake→excretion)",
    "Non-hypertensive K attenuation", "Whole-population LSS coverage sweep",
    "Packaged trend base year / ceiling / post-2030",
    "Fiscal base (tax / pass-through / elasticity / taxable share)"),
  Value = c(as.character(n_pri), as.character(RC$analysis_years[1]), "2019 (pre-pandemic)",
    paste0(SCALEUP_YEAR1, "–", SCALEUP_YEAR2), as.character(RC$analysis_years[2]),
    paste(RC$impact_years, collapse = ", "),
    "IHD, ischaemic stroke, intracerebral haemorrhage, hypertensive heart disease",
    "Discretionary, packaged, restaurant, public, inherent",
    "2.8 / 1.0 mmHg per g/day", "2 g/day (WHO)",
    paste0(pct(RC$lss$nacl_fraction, 0), " / ", pct(RC$lss$kcl_fraction, 0)),
    formatC(RC$lss$adherence, format = "f", digits = 2),
    formatC(RC$lss$uptake, format = "f", digits = 2),
    paste0("≈", formatC(RC$lss$k_per_g_kcl / RC$lss$na_per_g_nacl, format = "f", digits = 2), " g"),
    paste0(RC$lss$k_mg_per_mmol, " ; ÷", RC$lss$k_intake_to_excretion),
    paste0("×", formatC(RC$lss$nonhtn_factor, format = "f", digits = 2)),
    paste0(paste(round(100 * s2_reg$cov), collapse = ", "), "%"),
    paste0("base ", RC$euromonitor$base_year, "; ceiling ", pct(RC$euromonitor$ceiling, 0), "; ", .euro_post2030),
    paste0(pct(RC$fiscal$base$tax_rate, 0), " / ", pct(RC$fiscal$base$pass_through, 0), " / ",
           formatC(RC$fiscal$base$elasticity, format = "f", digits = 2), " / ", pct(RC$fiscal$base$taxable_share, 0))),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
add_tab("key_inputs", "Key model inputs and parameters", key_inputs,
  source = REPORT_SOURCE,
  notes = paste0("Initialization (", RC$analysis_years[1], ") establishes the first transition history; ",
    "2019 is the pre-pandemic epidemiologic seed/reference year; the model then projects annually to ",
    RC$analysis_years[2], "."))

# T: Benchmark (reuse bt_fmt if available) -----------------------------------
if (exists("benchmark_available") && isTRUE(benchmark_available) && exists("bt_fmt"))
  add_tab("benchmark", "Benchmark: current full package vs. previous 30% sodium-reduction estimate",
    as.data.frame(bt_fmt),
    units = "Millions of deaths delayed; percent of each model's own baseline",
    period = WINDOW, source = REPORT_SOURCE,
    notes = "Contextual comparison against the previous 100 Million Lives Saved estimate; scenarios and horizons are not fully equivalent.", fontsize = 8, orientation = "landscape")

# T: Huang & Saxena comparisons (reuse) --------------------------------------
if (exists("huang_cmp")) add_tab("huang", "Low-sodium salt substitute model vs. Huang et al. (2026)",
  huang_cmp, source = REPORT_SOURCE,
  notes = "Positions the mechanistic salt-substitute model against the global study whose structure it follows (Huang et al., 2026).",
  fontsize = 8, orientation = "landscape")
if (exists("saxena_cmp")) add_tab("saxena", "Fiscal model vs. Saxena et al. (2025)",
  saxena_cmp, source = REPORT_SOURCE,
  notes = "Positions the salt-tax model against the study that anchors it (Saxena et al., 2025).",
  fontsize = 8, orientation = "landscape")

cat("tr-tables-appendix: total tables =", length(TAB), "\n")
```

```{r tr-figures, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}
# ------------------------------------------------------------- tr-figures ----
# All figures are saved as 300-dpi PNGs into docs/report_assets/ and the plotted
# data is captured for the workbook. Schematic diagrams carry no data table.

mk_flow2 <- function(labels, fill = RTSL$lpurple3, border = RTSL$purple,
                     textcol = RTSL$text, tsize = 3.0) {
  n <- length(labels); bx <- data.table(x = seq_len(n), label = labels)
  ar <- data.table(x = (seq_len(n - 1)) + 0.46, xend = (2:n) - 0.46, y = 1, yend = 1)
  ggplot() +
    geom_tile(data = bx, aes(x = x, y = 1), width = 0.88, height = 0.7,
              fill = fill, color = border, linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_text(data = bx, aes(x = x, y = 1, label = label), size = tsize,
              lineheight = 0.95, colour = textcol) +
    geom_segment(data = ar, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend),
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.14, "cm"), type = "closed"),
                 linewidth = 0.5, color = RTSL$midgrey) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.5, n + 0.5), ylim = c(0.55, 1.45)) + theme_void(base_size = 11)
}

# f01: overall framework -----------------------------------------------------
p_f01 <- mk_flow2(c("Sodium sources\n(5 per country)", "Policy effects\n× source shares",
  "Total sodium\nreduction (η)", "Blood pressure\n(± potassium)", "CVD incidence\n(4 causes)",
  "Well→Sick→Dead\nstate transitions", "Deaths\ndelayed"), tsize = 2.7)
add_fig("framework", "Overall model framework: from policy to deaths delayed",
  basename(save_tr_fig(p_f01, "fig_tr_framework.png", 11, 2.2)), 11, 2.2,
  notes = paste0("Schematic of the causal chain shared by every policy. A policy ",
    "reduces sodium from the sources it can reach; lower average sodium (and, for salt ",
    "substitutes, higher potassium) lowers systolic blood pressure; lower blood pressure ",
    "reduces incidence of four cardiovascular diseases; and a well-sick-dead population ",
    "model converts the lower incidence into cardiovascular deaths delayed. η is the ",
    "total sodium-reduction fraction."),
  source = REPORT_SOURCE)

# f02: sodium-source & intervention map --------------------------------------
.map_ivs <- c("Public procurement", "Salt targets", "FOP labelling", "Fiscal (tax)", "LSS")
.map_srcs <- c("Discretionary", "Packaged", "Restaurant", "Public", "Inherent")
map_dt <- data.table(
  source = factor(rep(.map_srcs, each = length(.map_ivs)), levels = rev(.map_srcs)),
  intervention = factor(rep(.map_ivs, times = length(.map_srcs)), levels = .map_ivs))
hits <- rbind(
  data.table(source = "Public", intervention = "Public procurement"),
  data.table(source = "Packaged", intervention = "Salt targets"),
  data.table(source = "Packaged", intervention = "FOP labelling"),
  data.table(source = "Packaged", intervention = "Fiscal (tax)"),
  data.table(source = "Discretionary", intervention = "LSS"))
map_dt[, hit := "no"]
map_dt[hits, on = c("source", "intervention"), hit := "yes"]
p_f02 <- ggplot(map_dt, aes(intervention, source, fill = hit)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 1.2, width = 0.95, height = 0.95) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(no = RTSL$chartgrey, yes = RTSL$purple),
                    labels = c(no = "Not targeted", yes = "Targeted"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + tr_theme +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1), panel.grid = element_blank())
add_fig("map", "Which policy acts on which sodium source",
  basename(save_tr_fig(p_f02, "fig_tr_map.png", 8.5, 4)), 8.5, 4,
  notes = paste0("Each policy is applied only to the sodium sources it can plausibly ",
    "reach; inherent sodium (in unprocessed foods) is never targeted. When two policies ",
    "act on the same source their effects compose multiplicatively rather than adding."),
  source = REPORT_SOURCE)

# f03: source shares by country ----------------------------------------------
sl <- melt(ss_raw[, c("location", SODIUM_SOURCES), with = FALSE], id.vars = "location",
           variable.name = "source", value.name = "share")
sl[, location := factor(location, levels = rev(country_order))]
sl[, source := factor(source, levels = SODIUM_SOURCES)]
p_f03 <- ggplot(sl, aes(share, location, fill = source)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = rtsl_source_cols, labels = source_labels, breaks = SODIUM_SOURCES,
                    name = "Sodium source") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  labs(x = "Share of total sodium intake", y = NULL) + tr_theme
f03_data <- dcast(sl, location ~ source, value.var = "share")
add_fig("shares", "Sodium source shares by country",
  basename(save_tr_fig(p_f03, "fig_tr_shares.png", 8.5, 4.2)), 8.5, 4.2,
  data = as.data.frame(f03_data),
  units = "Share of total baseline sodium intake (rows sum to 100%)",
  period = paste0("Base year ", RC$euromonitor$base_year),
  notes = paste0("Base-year composition of sodium intake in each country, from the RTSL sodium ",
    "policy document. Countries where packaged food is large (e.g. China, Malaysia) favour ",
    "reformulation and labelling; countries where discretionary salt dominates (e.g. Ethiopia, ",
    "India, Bangladesh) favour salt substitutes. Nigeria's profile is applied to Cameroon ",
    "because a country-specific profile was unavailable."),
  source = REPORT_SOURCE)

# A 10-colour qualitative palette drawn entirely from the RTSL brand palette, used
# where a figure needs one colour per country (kept separable and on-brand).
rtsl_qual <- c(RTSL$purple, RTSL$orange, RTSL$dgreen, RTSL$red, RTSL$lpurple1,
               RTSL$gold, RTSL$lgreen, RTSL$yellow, RTSL$midgrey, RTSL$lpurple2)
country_pal <- setNames(rtsl_qual[seq_along(country_order)], country_order)

# f04: packaged share over time ----------------------------------------------
pk <- source_shares_by_year[location %in% country_order & year >= RC$euromonitor$base_year &
                            year <= impact_y2]
pk[, location := factor(location, levels = country_order)]
p_f04 <- ggplot(pk, aes(year, packaged, colour = location)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = RC$euromonitor$ceiling, linetype = "dashed", colour = RTSL$divider) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = country_pal, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Packaged share of total sodium") + tr_theme +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
add_fig("packaged_time", "Packaged share of sodium over time, by country",
  basename(save_tr_fig(p_f04, "fig_tr_packaged_time.png", 9, 4.2)), 9, 4.2,
  data = as.data.frame(dcast(pk[, .(location, year, packaged)], year ~ location, value.var = "packaged")),
  units = "Packaged food as a share of total sodium intake",
  period = paste0(RC$euromonitor$base_year, "–", impact_y2),
  notes = paste0("The packaged share follows a country-specific growth trend, capped at ",
    pct(RC$euromonitor$ceiling, 0), " (dashed line); after 2030 the share is ", .euro_post2030,
    ". Raising the packaged share is a compositional reallocation: the other four source ",
    "shares are rescaled proportionally so all five always sum to 100%. Total baseline sodium ",
    "intake does not grow; only its source composition changes. Trend from commercial sales ",
    "data (Euromonitor, Marklund)."),
  source = REPORT_SOURCE)

# f05: LSS Na/K pathway ------------------------------------------------------
p_f05 <- mk_flow2(c("Switch to LSS\n75% NaCl / 25% KCl", "↓ discretionary sodium\n+ ↑ potassium",
  "↓ SBP\nΔSBP(Na) + ΔSBP(K)", "↓ CVD incidence\nall four causes", "Deaths\ndelayed"),
  fill = "#E4F0E6", border = RTSL$dgreen, tsize = 2.7)
add_fig("lss_pathway", "Low-sodium salt substitute causal pathway (sodium and potassium to blood pressure)",
  basename(save_tr_fig(p_f05, "fig_tr_lss_pathway.png", 10.5, 2.1)), 10.5, 2.1,
  notes = paste0("Replacing discretionary salt with a low-sodium salt substitute both ",
    "removes sodium and adds potassium; each lowers systolic blood pressure through its own ",
    "dose-response, and the two blood-pressure changes are combined. This is a benefit-only ",
    "pathway: potential chronic-kidney-disease / hyperkalaemia harms of higher potassium are ",
    "not modelled."),
  source = REPORT_SOURCE)

# f_state: Well-Sick-Dead state-transition diagram (comment D) ---------------
# A faithful TikZ-style state diagram drawn with base ggplot geoms (no external
# .tex / tikzDevice, so it renders portably to a 300-dpi PNG for Word).
.box <- function(cx, cy, w, h, fill, border, label, tcol = RTSL$text, ts = 3.1) {
  list(
    rect = data.table(xmin = cx - w/2, xmax = cx + w/2, ymin = cy - h/2, ymax = cy + h/2,
                      fill = fill, border = border),
    txt  = data.table(x = cx, y = cy, label = label, tcol = tcol, ts = ts))
}
.boxes <- list(
  well = .box(1.3, 3.0, 1.6, 0.95, RTSL$lpurple3, RTSL$purple, "Well\n(healthy, at risk)"),
  sick = .box(4.2, 3.0, 1.6, 0.95, "#E4F0E6", RTSL$dgreen, "Sick\n(living with CVD)"),
  cvd  = .box(7.1, 3.0, 1.6, 0.95, "#FBDDD3", RTSL$orange, "CVD death\n(cause-specific)"),
  bg   = .box(4.2, 1.1, 1.9, 0.9,  RTSL$chartgrey, RTSL$midgrey, "Background death\n(other causes)"))
rects <- rbindlist(lapply(.boxes, `[[`, "rect"))
txts  <- rbindlist(lapply(.boxes, `[[`, "txt"))
# "Stacked cards" behind Sick and CVD boxes -> four independent cause processes.
shadow <- rbindlist(lapply(list(.boxes$sick$rect, .boxes$cvd$rect), function(r)
  rbind(data.table(xmin = r$xmin + 0.10, xmax = r$xmax + 0.10, ymin = r$ymin + 0.14,
                   ymax = r$ymax + 0.14, fill = r$fill, border = r$border),
        data.table(xmin = r$xmin + 0.20, xmax = r$xmax + 0.20, ymin = r$ymin + 0.28,
                   ymax = r$ymax + 0.28, fill = r$fill, border = r$border))))
arr <- arrow(length = unit(0.18, "cm"), type = "closed")
p_state <- ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = shadow, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = fill),
            colour = NA, linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_rect(data = rects, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax,
            fill = fill, colour = border), linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_identity() + scale_colour_identity() +
  geom_text(data = txts, aes(x, y, label = label), colour = RTSL$text,
            size = 3.2, lineheight = 0.95, fontface = "bold") +
  # Well -> Sick (incidence)
  annotate("segment", x = 2.1, xend = 3.4, y = 3.0, yend = 3.0, colour = RTSL$purple,
           linewidth = 0.8, arrow = arr) +
  annotate("text", x = 2.75, y = 3.35, label = "Incidence (IR)", size = 3.0, colour = RTSL$text) +
  # Sick -> CVD death (case fatality)
  annotate("segment", x = 5.0, xend = 6.3, y = 3.0, yend = 3.0, colour = RTSL$orange,
           linewidth = 0.8, arrow = arr) +
  annotate("text", x = 5.65, y = 3.35, label = "Case fatality (CF)", size = 3.0, colour = RTSL$text) +
  # Sick -> Background death (background mortality)
  annotate("segment", x = 4.2, xend = 4.2, y = 2.52, yend = 1.57, colour = RTSL$midgrey,
           linewidth = 0.8, arrow = arr) +
  # Well -> Background death (background mortality)
  annotate("curve", x = 1.3, xend = 3.25, y = 2.52, yend = 1.2, colour = RTSL$midgrey,
           linewidth = 0.8, curvature = 0.25, arrow = arr) +
  annotate("text", x = 5.55, y = 1.95, label = "Background\nmortality (m)", size = 3.0,
           colour = RTSL$text, lineheight = 0.9) +
  # Annual aging / cohort entry (curved loop above Well)
  annotate("curve", x = 0.75, xend = 1.85, y = 3.7, yend = 3.55, colour = RTSL$lpurple1,
           linewidth = 0.6, curvature = -0.6, arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.14, "cm"))) +
  annotate("text", x = 1.3, y = 4.05, label = "Age +1 yr each cycle; cohort enters at age 20",
           size = 2.7, colour = RTSL$midgrey) +
  annotate("text", x = 7.1, y = 1.7, label = "× 4 independent\ncause processes", size = 2.7,
           colour = RTSL$midgrey, fontface = "italic", lineheight = 0.9) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.2, 8.1), ylim = c(0.5, 4.3)) + theme_void()
add_fig("state_transition", "Well–sick–dead state-transition model",
  basename(save_tr_fig(p_state, "fig_tr_state_transition.png", 10, 3.2)), 10, 3.2,
  notes = paste0("Each year, well (healthy) people develop disease at the incidence rate ",
    "(IR); people living with disease may die of it at the case-fatality rate (CF); and both ",
    "groups are subject to background mortality (m) from other causes. The surviving ",
    "population ages by one year and a new cohort enters at age 20. The process runs ",
    "independently for each of four causes (ischaemic heart disease, ischaemic stroke, ",
    "intracerebral haemorrhage, hypertensive heart disease), shown by the stacked boxes. ",
    "Sodium policies lower IR (not CF); running the model with and without a policy and ",
    "differencing the deaths gives the cardiovascular deaths delayed."),
  source = REPORT_SOURCE)

# f06: headline deaths delayed by intervention -------------------------------
hl_scen <- c("public_procurement", "fopl", "salt_targets", "fiscal_base",
             "full_package", "lss_s4", "lss_s5", tail(s2_reg$scenario, 1))
hl_scen <- hl_scen[hl_scen %in% as.character(dd_cum$scenario)]
hl <- dd_cum[as.character(scenario) %in% hl_scen]
hl[, lab := factor(scenario_labels_short[as.character(scenario)],
                   levels = scenario_labels_short[as.character(hl[order(deaths_delayed), scenario])])]
p_f06 <- ggplot(hl, aes(deaths_delayed / 1e6, lab, fill = scenario)) +
```
